corrections.defectSummary: rcap-pdf-anchor-capture loadFonts never consults /ToUnicode or /Encoding /Differences, so a subset-font text layer decodes to nothing and a fillable form was dispositioned as having no extractable text.
corrections.fieldOrRegion: anchorCapture: 199 lines across 6 pages, readableLines 0 on every page
corrections.visibleDefect: The family is dispositioned "overlay_no_extractable_text_layer" and produced no fill, but the source does have a text layer: it draws 199 lines. The text is a subset font whose codes are offset (a +29 shift), and decoding it yields plain, usable content — e.g. page 1 of blake-006 reads "District/Municipal Court of Washington, County/City of ... No. ... Plaintiff ... Defendant ... DOB". So the stated premise ('no extractable text layer') is false, and a form that could have been anchored and overlaid was dropped.
corrections.likelyOwner: D0 shared factory — scripts/rcap-official-forms/rcap-pdf-anchor-capture.mjs, loadFonts(): it reads only Subtype/FirstChar/Widths/MissingWidth and never consults /ToUnicode or /Encoding /Differences, so content-stream byte codes are used verbatim as characters. Lane D1B's NC decoder shows the correct approach is available (source-record decodeBasis 'page_content_stream_tounicode_decoded_per_run', cmapsConsulted 9).
corrections.acceptanceCondition: loadFonts must build a code->unicode map from each font's /ToUnicode CMap (falling back to /Encoding /Differences and the standard encodings) and extractTextItems must emit decoded characters. After the fix, anchorCapture for blake-006 and blake-008 must report readableLines > 0 on every page, and each family must be re-dispositioned on the real anchor set rather than on 'no extractable text layer'.
